title: Haya preheated iron-smelting furnaces, Tanzania
summary: Research on the Haya of northwestern Tanzania, on the western shore of Lake Victoria, concluded in 1978 that these people and their forebears 1500 to 2000 years ago smelted iron in furnaces based on preheating principles. Anthropologist Peter Schmidt and metallurgy professor Donald Avery reported that the process produced carbon steel.

uncertainty.note: The 1978 abstract says '1500 to 2000 years ago'; the years -22 and 478 are 2000 and 1500 years before 1978, so the range is approximate. The preheating interpretation comes from Schmidt and Avery; other scholars' views were not opened.

where.modern_name: Kagera Region, northwestern Tanzania (region centre; labelled proxy pin for the Haya area west of Lake Victoria)
where.historical_name: Haya area, west shore of Lake Victoria (pre-colonial East Africa)

importance.justification: Argued to be an advanced iron-smelting technology in prehistoric East Africa, significant for the history of Africa and of metallurgy (Science, 1978).

reviewer_note: Replaces the unrelated Han-dynasty idea in the id: 'Haya' is the Haya people of Tanzania. The 1978 Science abstract (via PubMed) and a 1978 TIME article are the only pages opened; the preheating thesis is Schmidt and Avery's and was reportedly disputed (not opened, so not stated). Pin is the Kagera Region centre, a labelled proxy: the opened pages name no site. Dates are 'years ago' relative to 1978.
